description.narrative: CampaignIdea_CI1The project is about enhancing the participation of civil society, movements and ordinary citizens,especially thoseworst impacted by climate change in the development of the Nationally DeterminedContributions (NDCs) of global south countries. Revised NDCs are due in 2025, and for which allcountries are preparing now.Working with Oxfam and their partners who have been engaged in similar processes of people’sparticipation in NDCs, we would like to do the following:i.) CAN selected Nodes toenhance the capacity of its members, movements and wider civil societyorganisations in their regions to understand the NDC processes and enhance people’s participation inthese processes, and thereby strengthen the network.ii.) Convening of CAN nodes and Oxfam partners to share the experiences of participation in NDCprocesses. The purpose of this convening is to understand whether the process was inclusive, and thechallenges they faced and find ways to overcame.Climate Action Network (CAN) is a network ofover 2000 organisations in almost 150countries working toensure climate, social and racial justice – several of these are Oxfam Novib partners, such as AfricansRising, SAAPE, AIIP etc. CAN’s convening strength is mainly from its national and regional nodes whocoordinate the local and national civil society and bring the issues to global policy fora such as theUNFCCC sessions. CAN have 25 National and Regional Nodes the project will work in 4 regional Nodesdirectly and other Nodes will participate in theprocess.The following activities will be implemented:i.)Enhancing engagement of civil society and people’s participation in the NDC processes. Thiswould broadly be a set of the following activities:a. Four global south nodes from Africa, Asia and Latin America will be selected for theimplementation of this project. They will be chosen on the basis of demonstrating how well they canmobilise the local communities they work with for participation in NDC processes, their connect with local,provincial and national government officials and how inclusive they can be in the kinds of communityvoices they can mobilise.b. Capacity building of CSOs in the chosen countries on NDC processes and how to engage in them.This will be held in partnership with Oxfam Novib and partners who have had prior experience on thesame.c. Engagement with community and local and national governance structures on NDCs: Severalcommunity meetings and consultations will be held by the chosen nodes with their members to enhanceawareness about NDCs. In addition, meetings with local and national government departments managingthe NDCprocess will also be held to ensure the participation of CSOs and people from affectedcommunities.d. Engaging in the NDC processes:The nodes will share informationabout planned stakeholderengagements as part of the NDC processes on a regular basis and encourage and accompany CSOrepresentatives, citizens esp. women, indigenous peoples and local communities worst affected by climatechange to share their insights during such meetings. In addition, information about people’s aspirations onhow climate change needs to be dealtwhile safeguarding their lives, homes, livelihoods and cultures willbe collected and shared wherever CSO submissions to the NDC process are possible.ii.) Online Convening in partnership with Oxfam: Oxfam Novib and their partners in a few countrieshave had the experience of engaging with the national governments on NDC processes. They alsoconducted a research study on the inclusiveness of NDC processes in 11 countries across the world. Inaddition, this study also documented their experience of active engagement in the NDC processes in 3other countries where they were present- Peru, Uganda and Burkina Faso. (In Uganda, they worked withCAN Uganda).Twoonline convenings will be held to cover the Western and Eastern time zones to ensure widerparticipation of CAN nodes across the board and cut down on costs. A further convening (if necessary) onhow to plan for community engagement on NDCs will be conducted with the four participant nodes.It is important for the participant nodes and their members to learn from this experience and build their planfor enhanced people’s participation and engagement in the NDC processes.Why this is a ‘sudden opportunity’(i.e., why your current budget is not able to cover it andwhy it was not included in your annual planning)SuddenOpportunity_CI2Global South nodes of CAN have low annual budgets, which are usually complemented by a meagre re-grant from CAN International via ourNode Development Fund (NDF). While several members have beenengaging with their governments on various climate policies and NDCs, wider participation of CSOs,movements and people has not been possible with the meagre funding available. This fundingwillcomplement our existing re-grant to the four nodes. The project will primarily involve re-granting to thenodes to support people’s and grassroots movements engagement in the NDC processes in their nodes.To share a few examples, CANLA has been bolstering thecapacity of its membership on engagement withgovernments on NDCs, adaptation, just transition etc. CANSEA has been active on Just Transition plans atcommunity level and would like to extend its work to the NDC engagement. CAN Southern Africa has hadsomesuccess in engagement with the Southern African Development Community (SADC) on Loss andDamage, as has CAN Western and Central Africa with their countries. CANSA has been regularlyengaging thegovernments in the South Asian region on resilience, adaptationand NDCs. As part of ournode strengthening and mobilisation, we are applying to various funders for bolstering the work in thenodes. However, a more ground level strengthening would provide the node and its members with thenecessary tools and skills toengage with the NDCs processes and complement their work on justtransition plans, adaptation plans etc. This opportunity is therefore a sudden and important opportunity forall the four nodes

participating-org.narrative:
Climate Action Network (CAN) is a global network of more than 1,900 civil society organisations in over 130 countries driving collective and sustainable action to fight the climate crisis and to achieve social justice. CAN convenes and coordinates civil society at the UN climate talks and other international fora.
Since its inception in the 1980s, CAN has grown into a strong, member-driven network with a membership spanning all six continents in over 130 countries.
With its diversity of membership and long-standing experience in steering the climate movement, CAN continues to seek alignment and build bridges with partners and stakeholders across theclimate movement and beyond to pressure governments to take bold and urgent climate action to end the era of fossil fuels and address the needs of the most vulnerable people impacted by the climate crisis.
Climate Action Network International functions as the Secretariat of the network and is independent legally and financially from any members and CAN nodes.
